description: The Creusot Squeeze Loop: annotates EXISTING Rust with Pearlite and proves it with `cargo creusot`, one function/unit at a time, so the loop converges on correct code-with-specs rather than a plausible-looking one. The requirement is external (transcription, A) but the Pearlite contracts that make it checkable are authored upstream by an actor that never sees the implementation (authored authority, B) — author independence carries the soundness argument. Dominant coherent-and-wrong: a vacuously-true / weaker-than-intended contract (#[ensures(true)], an unsatisfiable #[requires], a proof of an adjacent weaker property) that Why3 discharges while proving the wrong theorem. NOTE: this registry models the FULL loop, whose U is an EXTERNAL requirement (exogenous). The lightweight 3-agent appendix variant instead derives U from a summary of the code (endogenous) — there a PASS certifies self-consistency, not conformance; see docs/u-provenance-ledger.md.

sources.name: External requirement (plain English / standard / ticket)
sources.notes: the U of the full loop; the strongest claim the code must satisfy. If instead derived from a code summary (lightweight variant), this becomes endogenous and a PASS is self-consistency only.

sources.name: Public function signatures / documented surface
sources.notes: the public interface the spec author and verifier may see; carries no implementation body

sources.name: The existing Rust function bodies (pre-existing)
sources.notes: the code under test; barriered from the spec author and verifier (they must reason from the requirement + surface, never the body)

sources.name: Pearlite contracts (requires/ensures/invariant authored from the requirement)
sources.notes: the spec author's deliverable; the annotator's upper bound

sources.name: Proof scaffolding added to the original Rust (invariants, variants, ghost/snapshot, proof_assert!)
sources.notes: the implementation artifact; must be ABSENT from the spec author's and verifier's context (physical barrier)

sources.name: Adversarial properties + mutation probes authored from the requirement + surface
sources.notes: the acceptance evidence; must be ABSENT from the annotator's context so it cannot tune the code to them

sources.name: cargo creusot -> Creusot->Coma->Why3 -> SMT discharge (Proved ... checkmark)
sources.notes: the per-obligation discharge verdict; mechanical and interpretation-free, no actor can alter it

sources.name: Standing invariant: cargo test + standing proof count + determinism re-run
sources.notes: rerun every cycle; previously discharged VCs stay discharged, determinism re-run agrees (zero regression)

sources.name: Scripted mutation probe (flip a comparator, drop a +1, widen a bound)
sources.notes: the Gate C non-vacuity oracle: a mutation that violates the requirement MUST break the proof, else the spec is vacuous

sources.name: Creusot/Why3's actual behaviour on a construct (capability)
sources.notes: what WP/the provers actually do; the probe's and spec author's expressibility oracle

sources.name: Minimal Creusot/Why3 capability experiment (one claim, one recorded verdict)
sources.notes: pins one tool-behaviour claim before machinery is built on it

sources.name: Cross-provider / human reviewer judgment
sources.notes: audits the coordinator's own consolidated heuristics and the Gate A editorial faithfulness; no executable refuter

actors.name: Coordinator
actors.builds: Gate A approvals, sequencing, gap-doc adjudication, DONE verdicts

lower_bound.text: the machine gate output (why3find discharge logs, test + mutation results, standing-invariant re-run)

forbidden_moves: let a producer's self-report end an item

actors.name: Spec author
actors.builds: the Pearlite contracts (requires/ensures + the requirement's invariants) from the requirement, blind to the body

upper_bound.text: the external requirement + the public signatures

lower_bound.text: expressibility: each clause must be dischargeable by SOME Why3 mechanism

forbidden_moves: read or infer the implementation body

actors.name: Annotator (implementer)
actors.builds: internal proof scaffolding on the original Rust: #[invariant], #[variant], ghost/snapshot, intermediate proof_assert!, minimal proof-preserving refactor

lower_bound.text: cargo creusot discharge + the standing test/invariant suite

forbidden_moves: weaken a contract or a gate to land

actors.name: Exerciser / Verifier
actors.builds: adversarial properties + the mutation probes from requirement + surface only; runs cargo creusot fresh

upper_bound.text: the requirement's acceptance clauses + the documented public surface

lower_bound.text: what actually discharges/proves when run, and whether the mutation breaks the proof

forbidden_moves: read the implementation body or the annotator's diff
anchor the adversarial properties to implementation quirks

actors.name: Probe
actors.builds: minimal Creusot/Why3 capability experiments (does WP handle this construct? does this prover discharge?)

upper_bound.text: one design claim per probe, drawn from the requirement context

forbidden_moves: implement a fix (a probe writes a verdict, never a fix)

actors.name: Cross-provider / human reviewer (terminus)
actors.builds: the terminal review of what the loop cannot self-certify: the coordinator's own consolidated heuristics and the Gate A editorial faithfulness (a contract as a faithful reading of the requirement)

upper_bound.text: the external requirement: is the coordinator's heuristic / carve-out a faithful reading of it, or does it share the loop's blind spot?

lower_bound.text: no executable oracle — soft-vs-soft faithfulness has no hard refuter; this absence is why the reviewer is the terminus
lower_bound.absent_reason: a same-provider-family judge shares the author's blind spot (only partial disjointness); closed by a disjoint cross-provider or human reviewer, not a machine

forbidden_moves: count a same-provider-family judge as full disjointness

disjointness.rationale: The spec author holds the requirement (never the code); the annotator holds the contracts (never the adversarial properties); the verifier holds the requirement + the runnable oracle (never the code or the diff); the coordinator holds the requirement + gate output (never producing an artifact it grades). Intersection = Rust that both discharges contracts authored from the requirement AND survives adversarial properties derived independently from that same requirement — and no single actor can certify it alone.
disjointness.load_bearing_barrier: spec author and verifier are delegated from fresh, body-free contexts: the implementation body and the annotator's diff are physically absent, not merely off-limits by instruction

catchability.blind_spot: games a weak contract — writes code that satisfies a vacuous spec
catchability.via: adversarial properties + the Gate C mutation probe (a violating mutant must break the proof)
the mutation probe fires, and adversarial properties that SHOULD fail against a vacuous spec do not
Gate A judges the contracts against the requirement (amend/cut/sharpen)

catchability.blind_spot: anchors its adversarial properties to implementation quirks
catchability.via: structurally prevented by the barrier; the coordinator confirms each adversarial property derives from U

catchability.blind_spot: its own editorial (Gate A) judgment and its own consolidated heuristics
catchability.via: the coordinator's heuristics are audited by the verifier or a cross-provider/human reviewer — never self-audited (Gate S / disjoint base)

disjointness.terminus: human_reviewer — Gate A editorial faithfulness (is each contract a faithful reading of the requirement?) and the coordinator's own heuristics close at a cross-provider/human review; the requirement is exogenous, so the mechanical oracle carries the main soundness and the editorial residual is the only soft-side hole. In the lightweight variant (endogenous U) the whole loop is a self-consistency check and needs an external requirement before any conformance claim.
